children: LightPath reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $71.7 million, up 92.7% year-over-year, and fourth-quarter revenue of $21.2 million, up 73.8% from the prior-year quarter. The company posted fiscal 2026 gross profit of $25.8 million (36.0% of revenue) and a fourth-quarter gross profit of $8.3 million (39.4% of revenue), and ended the year with a record order backlog of approximately $110.9 million. LightPath closed a $50.0 million primary equity offering in June 2026 and reported cash and cash equivalents of $93.2 million at June 30, 2026.
Revenue — Fiscal 2026: $71.7 million; Three months ended June 30, 2026: $21.2 million.
Gross profit — Fiscal 2026: $25.8 million (36.0% of revenue); Q4 FY2026: $8.3 million (39.4% of revenue).
Operating loss — Q4 FY2026 operating loss: $(4.3) million; Fiscal 2026 operating loss: $(19.7) million.
Net loss — Q4 FY2026 net loss: $(4.14) million; Fiscal 2026 net loss: $(20.55) million.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) — Q4 FY2026: $2.10 million (10% of revenue); Fiscal 2026: $4.23 million (6% of revenue).
Order backlog reached a record $110.9 million at June 30, 2026, with approximately $85.6 million scheduled for delivery within the next 12 months.

Completed strategic acquisitions and manufacturing expansion: full-year contribution from G5 Infrared and partial-year contribution from Amorphous Materials, adding domestic glass production capacity and proprietary infrared compositions.

Onshoring and product strategy: continued shift toward germanium-free BlackDiamond™ glass portfolio (including NRL-licensed compositions) and expansion of melting capacity in Orlando and Texas to support projected demand.

Significant commercial wins and orders: received an $11 million follow-on infrared camera order from a global technology customer for counter-UAS applications and $13 million in follow-on optical assembly orders from a defense systems supplier.

Corporate and operational restructuring: signed definitive agreement to divest the China-based manufacturing subsidiary (LPOIZ) to transition to a Western-aligned manufacturing footprint and advanced redesign efforts to convert G5 Infrared camera products to BlackDiamond™ materials.
